You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From a5880b84430316e3e1c1f5d23aa32ec6000cc717 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Leon Romanovsky <leonro@mellanox.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Mar 2018 18:49:16 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] RDMA/ucma: Check that user doesn't overflow QP state

The QP state is limited and declared in enum ib_qp_state,
but ucma user was able to supply any possible (u32) value.

Reported-by: syzbot+0df1ab766f8924b1edba@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Fixes: 75216638572f ("RDMA/cma: Export rdma cm interface to userspace")
Signed-off-by: Leon Romanovsky <leonro@mellanox.com>
Signed-off-by: Doug Ledford <dledford@redhat.com>
---
 drivers/infiniband/core/ucma.c | 3 +++
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+)

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/core/ucma.c b/drivers/infiniband/core/ucma.c
index 1817dfea8345..3a9d0f5b5881 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/core/ucma.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/core/ucma.c
@@ -1149,6 +1149,9 @@ static ssize_t ucma_init_qp_attr(struct ucma_file *file,
 	if (copy_from_user(&cmd, inbuf, sizeof(cmd)))
 		return -EFAULT;
 
+	if (cmd.qp_state > IB_QPS_ERR)
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	ctx = ucma_get_ctx(file, cmd.id);
 	if (IS_ERR(ctx))
 		return PTR_ERR(ctx);
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the lack of validation for the user-supplied value for the QP (Queue Pair) state in the ucma_init_qp_attr function. Users were able to provide any 32-bit unsigned integer value, which could exceed the defined limits of the QP state as specified in the ib_qp_state enum. This oversight allowed invalid states to be set, potentially leading to undefined behavior or crashes in the RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access) subsystem. The patch adds a check to ensure that the provided QP state does not exceed the maximum valid state (IB_QPS_ERR), thus preventing overflow and ensuring that only valid states are accepted.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:
    Code statements:
    <text1>
    <text2>
    <text3>
    <text4>
    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the lack of validation for the user-supplied value for the QP (Queue Pair) state in the ucma_init_qp_attr function. Users were able to provide any 32-bit unsigned integer value, which could exceed the defined limits of the QP state as specified in the ib_qp_state enum. This oversight allowed invalid states to be set, potentially leading to undefined behavior or crashes in the RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access) subsystem. The patch adds a check to ensure that the provided QP state does not exceed the maximum valid state (IB_QPS_ERR), thus preventing overflow and ensuring that only valid states are accepted.
